statement: Whenever count_pairs root distance returns Ok r, r equals the number of unordered pairs {u,v} of two distinct leaf positions u and v of root such that the length, counted in edges, of the unique simple path between u and v in root is at most distance. A leaf position is a node occurrence of the form Node(val, Null, Null); distinct leaf positions may have equal stored values.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least 1 and at most 1024 nodes; every Node value in root lies in [1,100]; distance is an i64 satisfying 1 <= distance <= 10.

statement: count_pairs root distance returns Ok r for some i64 r; in particular it does not return Err, overflow, go out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least 1 and at most 1024 nodes; every Node value in root lies in [1,100]; distance is an i64 satisfying 1 <= distance <= 10.

statement: Whenever count_pairs root d1 returns Ok r1 and count_pairs root d2 returns Ok r2, r1 <= r2.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least 1 and at most 1024 nodes; every Node value in root lies in [1,100]; d1 and d2 are i64 with 1 <= d1 <= d2 <= 10.

statement: Whenever count_pairs root1 distance returns Ok r1 and count_pairs root2 distance returns Ok r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: root1 and root2 are finite binary trees with at least 1 and at most 1024 nodes each; every Node value in both trees lies in [1,100]; root1 and root2 have the same underlying shape, meaning root2 is obtained from root1 by replacing each stored node value while keeping every Null/Node constructor and every parent-child position unchanged; distance is an i64 satisfying 1 <= distance <= 10.
